This codebook will help you extract just the structured text from Nexis Uni and exclude the metadata that is causing fits with your sentiment analysis, topic models etc.


```{r include: false}
#| include: false
# 1. Load the relevant software libraries

library(tidyverse)
library(tidytext)
library(rio)
library(googlesheets4)
library(janitor)
```
### Import large DF from a Google Drive
```{r}
gs4_deauth()
text <- read_sheet(
  "https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1y7oTIJ8vpxswZMjlWG65mqnssJl_g3dwssC_wiCeylQ/edit?usp=sharing",
  col_types = "nccccccccccccccccccccccccc" # Adjust letters to match your exact column order (n = numeric, c = character)
) |>
  clean_names() |>
  as.data.frame()

```


# Clean and extract just the body text
Thanks to Zirong for this idea

```{r}
#set your beginning and end points here
begin <- "Body"
end <- "End of Document"

text_clean <- text |> 
  mutate(sentence = str_squish(sentence)) |> 
  group_by(filename) |>
  mutate(
    line       = row_number(),
    # body starts after the "Body" line (defaults to 0 if "Body" isn't found)
    body_start = coalesce(which(sentence == begin)[1], 0L),
    # body ends at "End of Document" (or end of group if not found)
    body_end   = coalesce(which(str_detect(sentence, regex(end, ignore_case = TRUE)))[1], n() + 1L)
  ) |>
  filter(line > body_start, line < body_end) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(!is.na(sentence), sentence != "") |>
  # cuts any leftover boilerplate lines inside the body
  filter(!str_detect(sentence, regex(paste(
    "^Link to (image|the original story)",
    "^Access PDF version",
    "^Click here for updates",
    "^ABSTRACT$",
    "^Dive Brief:?$",
    "^\\[Sign up for",
    "^For the latest news, weather",
    "^Correction",
    "^Update \\d",
    "^_+$",
    "^Photo:",
    "^TM & ©",
    "Copyright|All rights reserved",
    sep = "|"), ignore_case = TRUE))) |>
  # drop short byline lines like "By Deidre McPhillips, CNN"
  filter(!(str_detect(sentence, "^By [A-Z]") & str_length(sentence) < 60)) |>
  # strip the Newstex prefix and any URLs sequentially on 'sentence'
  mutate(
    sentence = str_remove(sentence, "^.*Delivered by Newstex\\)\\s*"),
    sentence = str_remove_all(sentence, "https?://\\S+|www\\.\\S+")
  ) |>
  select(-line, -body_start, -body_end)

```



#validate
```{r}
text |> 
  distinct(filename) |> 
  count()

text_clean |> 
  distinct(filename) |> 
  count()

```

  n_distinct()

#Cleaning junk

```{r}
#4. Remove useless metadata such as "Los Angeles Times" and "ISSN". See sample code below
China_cleaned <- RawChinaData %>%
  mutate(text = str_squish(text)) %>% #gets rid of leading and trailing spaces + double spaces
  mutate(text = tolower(text)) %>%
  mutate(text = str_replace(text, "startofarticle", "")) %>%
  mutate(text = gsub("issn:\\s+\\S+", "", text)) %>%
 mutate(text = str_remove_all(text, "https?://\\S+")) |> 
  mutate(text = str_remove_all(text, "\\d{2}\\s+[a-z]{3,9}\\s+\\d{4}(?:[:;,\\.\\s]+[a-z]\\.\\d+)?")) %>%
  mutate(text = str_remove_all(text, "[:;,\\.\\[\\]]")) %>%
  mutate(text = str_replace_all(text, c(
    "copyright" = "",
    "database: proquest central" = "",
    "language of publication: english" = "",
    "document url:\\s+\\S+" = "",
    "proquest document id:\\s+\\S+" = "",
    "publication subject:\\s+\\S+" = "",
    "publication date:\\s+\\S+" = "",
    "pages:\\s+\\S+" = "",
    "publication info" = "",
    "last updated:\\s+\\S+" = "",
    "interest periodicals--united states" = "",
    "https://+/docview/\\d+\\?accountid=\\d+" =""
  ))) %>%
  mutate(text = str_replace_all(text, c(
    "search.proquest.com" = "",
    "los angeles times" = "",
    "los angeles" = "",
    "calif" = ""))) 

```
